questions: Did line_loss_events on s-bend and slalom fall below the iteration 1 values of 1.3 and 1.1 per run? Report the count per track.
Did max_error on s-bend and slalom fall below 0.06 m, and how many runs still ended off-track? Report off-track counts per track.
Did the oval finish rate stay at or above 13 of 20, with completion_time near 1.8 s?
Did the forward position change steering_oscillation, and does the oval oscillation still look like a weight problem?
If line-loss is unchanged at y = 0.07, do you think the next lever should be a narrower wheel_track (0.10 m) or lower weights?

intent: Test whether moving the ±0.03 m, 0.015 m-spaced, 0.012 m-footprint sensor row forward from y = 0.06 m to y = 0.07 m (more look-ahead) reduces line loss on bends, with every other geometry value held at the iteration 1 best. The Integrator should keep the controller as in iteration 1 so this race isolates the forward position. The oval steering_oscillation of about 0.31 is a weight question for the Integrator, not a geometry one.
learning: Iteration 3 showed that footprint overlap at 0.016 m costs oval finishes without fixing line loss, so footprint is not the gap. Iterations 0 and 1 suggest that forward position (0.04 to 0.06 m) matters, though they were confounded with other changes. This race tests forward position alone against the best-known geometry.
rationale: Evidence so far. Iteration 1 (span ±0.03 m at 0.015 m spacing, 0.012 m footprint, y = 0.06 m) is still the best result at 337.5, with 13/20 oval finishes. Iteration 2 (span ±0.04 m at 0.02 m spacing) fell to 150.8 with 0/20 oval finishes, so widening the span hurt. Iteration 3 (±0.03 m, 0.015 m spacing, footprint raised to 0.016 m) fell to 217.4. Oval finishes dropped from 13/20 to 2/20, and slalom line-loss rose to 1.85 per run. Footprint overlap therefore did not close the line-loss gap and cost oval performance, so I am not keeping 0.016 m. The Integrator's feedback for this candidate recommends 0.016 m, but it was written before iteration 3 raced and its own evidence contradicts that recommendation, so I am not following it. The remaining evidence is that the line is lost on bends (1.1 to 1.3 line-loss events per run on s-bend and slalom, max_error 0.062 to 0.063 m), not from speed (oval completes in 1.83 s), and neither span nor footprint fixes it. Iteration 0 (y = 0.04) was the worst geometry and iteration 1 (y = 0.06) the best, so sensor forward position is the one geometry lever the evidence points to that has not been tested alone. Change this iteration: return to the iteration 1 geometry (best 337.5, 0.012 m footprint, 0.015 m spacing, ±0.03 m span, wheel_track 0.11, mass 0.7, wheel_radius 0.03, body unchanged) and move the sensor row forward from y = 0.06 to y = 0.07 m. This gives more look-ahead so the steering reacts before the robot reaches 0.06 m off the line. Expected result: line-loss events on s-bend and slalom fall toward 0.5 to 1.0 per run and max_error drops below about 0.055 m, with the oval finish rate held at about 13/20. If y = 0.07 does not change line-loss, the forward position is not the gap and the next test should be a narrower wheel_track for turn authority.
